lesson_title: Settlement, Economy and Mapwork Essentials: The Paper 2 Revision Sweep
hook_text: One taxi ride explains half of Paper 2. Watch the village empty and the city grow — with every exam term named.
clip_script: Now watch cousin Sipho leave. The farm mechanised and shed its workers — push. Johannesburg's wages, real and rumoured, called — pull. That single taxi ride is rural-urban migration, and repeated ten thousand times it becomes rural depopulation: the village school loses learners until it closes, the clinic follows, the shop cannot keep its doors open because its threshold — the minimum number of customers it needs — has left for Gauteng. Sipho lands in the city and reads it like a map: the CBD on the dearest land, the transition zone gone shabby, the malls that fled to the highways, and far out, past the old buffer strips, the township — the South African city model, drawn not by markets alone but by history.
visual_style: Animated journey line from a nucleated village across the map to Johannesburg: houses greying out behind, city zones lighting up ahead, each exam term stamping on screen as it is named — PUSH, PULL, THRESHOLD, BUFFER ZONE.
mood: Documentary storytelling, human and grounded, exam-sharp.
pacing: Steady narrative build through the journey, quick-fire term stamps, reflective close on the city skyline.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and turn the story you already know into Paper 2 marks.
